symptom: On the after-startup runner (Docker, `--local --legacy-runner`) two tests in one file that both assign the same variable with a lower-case keyword — `$r = call microflow …`, mdl 1's and `fmt`'s spelling — fail injection with MDL063 (CE0111 "Duplicate variable name" from mxbuild); the same file runs under the endpoint runner, which gives each test its own flow
cause: The legacy runner compiles every test into one microflow and renames each test's variables with a `_N` suffix, but which variables to rename was decided by `assignPattern`, which matched only upper-case `CALL|CREATE` — the spelling of the runner's own early examples. A lower-case assignment was left unrenamed and declared once per test
insight: The cheapest detector was a sweep, not a reading: every `.test.mdl` in the repo through `GenerateTestRunner` and `executor.ValidateProgram` — 10 of the 16 in mdl-examples/ drew MDL063 before the fix, 2 after. Those 2 (`retrieve $Brands`, `retrieve $Request` + `$Request = head(…)`) are the remaining, separate gap: `assignPattern` never matched `retrieve $x`, `declare $x`, list operations (`$x = filter(…)`), `send rest request` or `execute database query` in ANY case, so a variable those define in two tests still collides; the durable fix is to take the declared names from the parsed body (`visitor.FlowStatements`, as `attachOnError` already does), not a regex. Two existing tests (`TestThrowsCatchesEveryCallKind`, `TestVerdictCatchesEveryCallKind`) matched the legacy output against the unrenamed lower-case statement and passed only because of the defect — a test that asserts a generator's text verbatim can encode the bug it should catch. The `\b` matters once the match is case-insensitive (`$r = callback`). Found alongside ako/mxcli#1753, whose bug-test therefore uses a distinct variable per test
